sources.title: How Claude remembers your project: Claude reads CLAUDE.md files at the start of every session; Claude treats them as context, not enforced configuration; to block an action regardless of what Claude decides, use a PreToolUse hook; target under 200 lines per CLAUDE.md file; files over 200 lines consume more context and may reduce adherence; run /init to generate a starting CLAUDE.md

beats.spoken: Does Claude Code get better the longer your CLAUDE.md is? I ran a short and a long version against each other.

The short version has four rules. One of them is a check rule: every answer ends with the line Rule 120 followed. If that line shows up at the end, Claude followed the rule. According to the docs, files over 200 lines use more context and may be followed less well.

data.quote: Files over 200 lines consume more context and may reduce adherence.
data.translation: Over 200 lines: more context, maybe less adherence.

beats.spoken: The long version has 240 rules, spread over fifteen topics like tests, logging and naming. The same check rule sits in the middle, as rule 120. Everything else in it is filler, written only for this test.
Run one, short version. Claude found the file, read it and ended with Rule 120 followed. It said eleven customers, though. The file has twelve, and the second repetition said twelve.
Run two, long version. Same tools, the same Glob and Read, twelve customers this time, and again the answer ended with Rule 120 followed.

Both runs ran twice, and the rule was followed every time. The difference is cost: with the long file, Claude read about twice as many tokens. The docs advise keeping the file short and moving procedures into skills.

data.headline: Input tokens per run
data.note: Keep it short, move procedures into skills (per the docs).

beats.spoken: Here, longer was not better, just more expensive. Follow Promptwerk for more Claude workflows, step by step.

data.statement: Longer was not better here, just costlier.
